newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares slip, sentiment remains buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares slip, sentiment remains buoyant.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.37 percent on Wednesday as investors continued to take profits out of a recent rally, but traders said the decline was unlikely to extend into the next week.
"There may be some small corrections but nothing dramatic is expected," Milos Pelcar of A banka said.
The 10-share SBI index fell 4.73 points to 1,283.0, but managed to stay 4.54 percent above its value a week ago.
"Some major shares have obviously reached limits that even foreign investors are not willing to cross, but I think the downturn will not continue," Pelcar said.
Turnover rose to 557.7 million tolars from 394.8 million. Overall five shares fell, nine rose and two remained unchanged, while another nine were untraded.
Drug maker Lek's A issue was again the most active share, falling 1.49 percent to 24,510 tolars on volume of 16,458 shares for total turnover of 417.9 million tolars.
"It appears that 25,000 tolars is proving to be a resistance," Pelcar added.
Port Luka Koper was the leading decliner, falling 2.29 percent to 2,050 tolars on volume of 993 shares.
Trading company Kovinotehna was the day's biggest gainer, rising seven percent to 428 tolars on volume of 19,736 shares.
